Mahapurusha from the Moon (Phaladeepika Ch.6; Saravali Ch.38). Mantreshwara and Kalyana-Varma read the five Mahapurusha yogas from the Chandra-lagna as well as the Lagna: a yogadhipati in own/exalted/mooltrikona dignity placed in a kendra from the Moon gives the yoga, governing mental inclinations. When angular from both Lagna and Moon the yoga is doubly strong (emperor-tier). Surfaced as distinct rules so the report can show the from-Moon reading separately from the canonical from-Lagna base.

Jupiter in a kendra (1/4/7/10) from the Moon. Confers fame, intelligence, and renown like the king of beasts (gaja-kesari = elephant-lion). Cancelled when either luminary is debilitated.
Supreme Gajakesari (Phaladeepika 6.10): Jupiter in kendra from Moon AND Jupiter is exalted. Strongest classical Gajakesari tier; supreme intellectual fame.

Strong Gajakesari (Phaladeepika 6.10 commentary): Jupiter in kendra from Moon AND Jupiter in own sign (Sagittarius/Pisces). Second tier of classical strength — distinct from the supreme exalted variant.
Gajakesari bhanga (Phaladeepika 6.11): base Gajakesari forms but Jupiter is combust or retrograde. The yoga is present but the fame/intellect is mixed or delayed.

Broad Sunapha: any planet (other than Sun) in 2nd from Moon. Confers self-earned wealth, dignity, and good name. The strict variant (`SUNAPHA_STRICT` in `miscellaneous.yogas`) requires a benefic AND nothing in 12th. The 5 per-planet sub-variants below give Phaladeepika 13.4 distinct effects.

Sunapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.4 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 2nd from Moon. Mars in 2nd from Moon — earnings through valor, military or technical leadership; surgeon, athlete, commander.

Sunapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.4 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 2nd from Moon. Mercury in 2nd from Moon — earnings through speech, learning, writing, trade, or analytical work; scholar, merchant, accountant.

Sunapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.4 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 2nd from Moon. Jupiter in 2nd from Moon — earnings through teaching, dharma, advisory, or priesthood; counsellor, judge, philosopher.

Sunapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.4 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 2nd from Moon. Venus in 2nd from Moon — earnings through arts, beauty, luxury, or relationships; artist, designer, diplomat, dealer in fine goods.

Sunapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.4 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 2nd from Moon. Saturn in 2nd from Moon — earnings through service, labor, durable goods, mining, or long-cycle disciplines; engineer, administrator, ascetic-worker.

Broad Anapha: any planet (other than Sun) in 12th from Moon. Confers refinement, eloquence, and inherited wealth. The strict variant lives in `miscellaneous.yogas` as `ANAPHA_STRICT`. The 5 per-planet sub-variants give Phaladeepika 13.5 distinct effects.

Anapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.5 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 12th from Moon. Mars in 12th from Moon — refined courage and physical bearing; subject is composed, surgical in action.

Anapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.5 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 12th from Moon. Mercury in 12th from Moon — refined intellect, eloquent speech, polished communication.

Anapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.5 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 12th from Moon. Jupiter in 12th from Moon — refined wisdom, charitable disposition, spiritual depth.

Anapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.5 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 12th from Moon. Venus in 12th from Moon — refined aesthetic sense, conjugal grace, inherited refinement.

Anapha sub-variants per Phaladeepika 13.5 — distinct effects per planet (other than Sun) occupying the 12th from Moon. Saturn in 12th from Moon — refined discipline, ascetic temperament, longevity of bearing.

Broad Durudhara: planets (other than Sun) in BOTH 2nd and 12th from Moon — combined Sunapha+Anapha. Confers all-round prosperity, good speech, and protection. Strongest of the three Moon-axis broad yogas. The strict benefic-only variant lives in `miscellaneous.yogas` as `DURUDHURA_STRICT`.
Adhi Yoga (Phaladeepika 6.16): benefics occupy the 6th, 7th, and 8th from Moon. Confers leadership, authority, and protection from enemies — "the yoga of supremacy".
Lakshmi Yoga (Phaladeepika 6.18): lord of 9th in own/exalted sign in kendra or trikona AND Moon strong. Grants extraordinary wealth, righteousness, and the favour of Lakshmi.

Kahala Yoga (Phaladeepika 6.14): lords of 4th and 9th in mutual exchange or kendra-relation while Lagna-lord is strong. Grants command of armies, lands, and household authority — "the yoga of the war-drum". Moon-conditioned variant: Moon strong supports the formation.
Shubha Kartari Yoga (Phaladeepika 6.17): benefics flank the Moon in both 2nd and 12th — Moon hemmed by benefics. Grants protection, refined disposition, and gradual rise.
Papa Kartari Yoga around Moon (Phaladeepika 6.17 inverse): malefics flank the Moon in both 2nd and 12th. Threatens emotional vulnerability and obstacles unless mitigated by strong Lagna-lord aspect.

Parvata Yoga (Phaladeepika 6.13): kendras occupied by benefics with the 6th and 8th vacant. Confers high status, leadership, and learning. Moon-conditioned variant: Moon in kendra strengthens the yoga.
Chandra in trikona aspected by a benefic — confers emotional steadiness, mother's welfare, and gradual prosperity. BPHS Ch.34 v.12 commentary.
Strong Chandra-Lagna combination (BPHS Ch.34 v.15): Moon in Lagna with a benefic in a kendra from Moon. Grants charisma, fame, and supportive companionship.
Broad Vesi: ANY planet (not only benefics) in 2nd from Sun. Distinct from the canonical benefic-only `VESI` in `surya.yogas` per Brihat Jataka 13.1 broad reading.
Broad Vosi: ANY planet (not only benefics) in 12th from Sun. Distinct from the canonical benefic-only `VOSI` in `surya.yogas` per Brihat Jataka 13.2 broad reading.
Broad Ubhayachari: ANY planet (not only benefics) on both sides of the Sun. Distinct from the canonical benefic-only `UBHAYACHARI` in `surya.yogas` per Brihat Jataka 13.3 broad reading.

Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus all in kendras or trikonas — confers extraordinary learning, eloquence, and the favour of the goddess Saraswati. Strongest indicator of intellectual/artistic eminence in the chart.

Moon and Mars conjunct in any sign — combination of mind (Moon) and energy (Mars) confers business acumen and earnings through enterprise. Modern interpretation often associates with self-made wealth.

Moon in 6th, 8th, or 12th from Jupiter (without being in a kendra from Lagna). The "cart wheel" yoga — fortunes rise and fall like a wheel. Cancelled when Moon is in a kendra from Lagna (Saravali variant).
Benefics occupy ALL four upachaya houses (3, 6, 10, 11) from the Moon. Confers wealth and earned prosperity — vasu-mati = "rich in wealth". Strong indicator of growing fortune through the lifespan.

Moon in own sign (Cancer) or exaltation (Taurus) placed in a kendra. The "nectar" yoga — confers emotional stability, longevity of mother, and unfailing protection. Strongest classical Moon configuration.
Moon in a kendra and Lagna-lord in a kendra. The "abundant" yoga — confers comprehensive prosperity, status, and physical well-being. Extends Amrit Yoga via Lagna-lord support.
Moon in dusthana (6th, 8th, or 12th) from Lagna. Threatens emotional and material poverty. Cancelled when Moon is exalted (Taurus) or in own sign (Cancer), even within the dusthana.
Sun and Mercury conjunct in any sign — confers intellect, eloquence, and royal favour. Strength is contingent on Mercury not being combust (within 14° of Sun).

Primary Kahala Yoga: Lagna-lord exalted AND 4th-lord in own/exalted dignity. Distinct from the existing `KAHALA` (raja-advanced) which only requires 4th-lord and 9th-lord both in kendras. The "kettle-drum" yoga indicating martial leadership; Phaladeepika lists Lagna-lord exaltation as the strongest form.

Full classical form requires 4-level dispositor chain (each lord's dispositor strong); Phase 2.1 captures the canonical Lagna+9th-lord dignity trigger.

Trikona-lord (5th — purva-punya) occupying Lagna. Confers intelligence, fame, and progeny — past-life merit blesses the self directly.
Trikona-lord (9th — bhagya/dharma) occupying Lagna. Confers good fortune, paternal blessing, and dharmic alignment of the self.
9th lord in 10th house — Dharma-Karmadhipati Yoga (placement form, distinct from the exchange form). Career rises directly from dharma; the strongest classical placement-only Raja Yoga.
10th lord in 9th house — mirror of 9-in-10 Dharma-Karmadhipati. Career serves dharma; status carries spiritual responsibility. Both directions of the 9-10 swap are classical Raja Yogas.

A pure (amala) benefic in the 10th house from Lagna or Moon. Confers a spotless reputation, fame, and lasting glory — the karma-bhava is unblemished. Phase 2.1 will split into Amala-from-Lagna and Amala-from-Moon variants per Phaladeepika.

Benefics simultaneously in 6th, 7th, and 8th from Moon. Confers leadership, eminence, and victory over enemies. The benefic envelopment of the Moon's adversarial axis flips affliction into ascendancy.
Lagna-lord in own/exalted dignity in a kendra, plus Jupiter aspecting Lagna. The "royal fan" yoga — confers the regal authority symbolised by the chamara fans waved beside enthroned kings.

Jupiter and Venus in kendras with no malefic in any kendra. The "mountain" yoga — confers towering wealth, scholarship, and eloquence. Among the rare classical yogas requiring zero malefic kendra-occupation.
Lords of 4th and 9th simultaneously in kendras. Confers vehicles, prosperity, and command over armies. The "kettledrum" yoga signifying martial leadership.
Benefic in 2nd from Sun (excluding Moon), with no other planet in 12th. Confers leadership, integrity, and steady speech. Per-planet sub-variants follow per Phaladeepika 6.18-6.22.
Benefic in 12th from Sun (excluding Moon), with no other planet in 2nd. Confers learning, generosity, and refined speech. Per-planet sub-variants follow per Phaladeepika 6.23-6.27.
Benefics in both 2nd and 12th from Sun. Confers all-round prosperity, dignity, and protection from enemies — the strongest of the Sun-axis yogas.

Vesi sub-variants per Phaladeepika 6.18-6.22 — distinct effects per benefic in 2nd from Sun, with the 12th vacant. The strict canonical reading restricts to natural benefics excluding Moon. Mars in 2nd from Sun (12th vacant) — confers martial valor that protects the soul-significator; commanding presence and direct speech.

Vesi sub-variants per Phaladeepika 6.18-6.22 — distinct effects per benefic in 2nd from Sun, with the 12th vacant. The strict canonical reading restricts to natural benefics excluding Moon. Mercury in 2nd from Sun (12th vacant) — clear intellect, persuasive speech, statesman-like authority.

Sun and Mercury conjunct in a kendra — strengthened variant of Budhaditya. Cancelled when Mercury is debilitated (Pisces) since the karaka of intellect loses dignity.
Sun flanked by benefics in 2nd and 12th from itself. Confers protection of the soul-significator and steady authority.
Sun flanked by malefics in 2nd and 12th from itself. Threatens the soul-significator with afflictions to status and father.
Sun in Aries (its sign of exaltation) placed in the 10th — Digbala plus exaltation in karma-bhava. One of the strongest indicators of public authority and government favour.
Lords of dhana-bhava (2nd) and labha-bhava (11th) both occupy kendras — confluence of accumulated and earned wealth in angular strength.
Lakshmi Yoga: lords of poorva-punya (5th) and bhagya (9th) both in kendras. Strongest classical wealth-and-fortune yoga, tied directly to the goddess Lakshmi.
Jupiter — natural karaka of wealth and abundance — in dhana-bhava (2nd) or poorva-punya (5th). Confers steady accumulation and access to family/inheritance wealth.
Venus — karaka of luxury, refinement, and Lakshmi — placed in dhana-bhava (2nd). Confers wealth through artistic/luxury endeavours and conjugal prosperity.
Mutual exchange (parivartana) of 2nd-lord and 11th-lord. Direct linkage between accumulated wealth and earned gains — sustained income flow.
9th lord (lord of fortune/dharma) occupying its own house. The "lord-in-own-house" rule grants Bhava Bala to the 9th, lifting fortune and paternal dharma in the chart.
Mutual exchange (parivartana) of Lagna-lord and 2nd-lord. Direct linkage between self and accumulated wealth — wealth follows the native rather than being separately earned.

Shringataka (water-chestnut / triangle) Akriti: all 7 grahas in trikonas (1+5+9). Confers leadership, fortune, and dharmic eminence — the strongest of the Akriti yogas.
Hala (plough) Akriti: all 7 grahas in 2+6+10 (panaphara-trikonas). Confers agricultural prosperity, hard-won wealth through labour. Two other Hala variants (3+7+11 and 4+8+12) are listed below.

Yupa (sacrificial post) Akriti: all 7 grahas in the first four houses (1+2+3+4). Confers ritual eminence, dharmic authority, and sacrificial-life dispositions.
Ishu (arrow) Akriti: all 7 grahas in 4+5+6+7. Confers sharpness of intellect, military / hunting professions, decisive action.
Sakti (spear) Akriti: all 7 grahas in 7+8+9+10. Confers power, authority via dharmic effort, late-life status.
Danda (staff) Akriti: all 7 grahas in 10+11+12+1. Distinct from the named-classical `DANDA` rule. Threatens punitive challenges in early life.

Naukha (boat) Akriti: all 7 grahas in houses 1-7 contiguous (i.e. spanning 1-2-3-4-5-6-7). Confers seafaring or trading professions, water-related fortune. Some sources count only 7 contiguous houses anywhere; this rule pins it to 1-7 per BPHS.

Kuta (peak/summit) Akriti: all 7 grahas in 7 consecutive houses starting from the 4th (4,5,6,7,8,9,10) — the descendent-arc counterpart to Nauka (1..7), Chatra (7..1), and Chapa (10..4). Distinct from Ishu (4 consecutive from 4th: 4,5,6,7).

Chatra (umbrella) Akriti: all 7 grahas in 7 consecutive houses starting from the 7th (7,8,9,10,11,12,1) — the "umbrella" arc spanning the descendant to the ascendant via the upper half. The first-quadrant counterpart is Nauka (1..7). Confers protective royal patronage.

Chapa (bow) Akriti: all 7 grahas in 7 consecutive houses starting from the 10th (10,11,12,1,2,3,4) — the meridian-to-IC arc. The fourth and last of the 7-house-arc quartet: Nauka (1..7), Kuta (4..10), Chatra (7..1), Chapa (10..4). Confers archery / hunting / military professions.

Ardha-Chandra (half-moon) Akriti: all 7 grahas span 7 contiguous houses starting from a panaphara (2/5/8/11) or apoklima (3/6/9/12) — distinct from the four kendra-start arcs (Nauka/Kuta/Chatra/Chapa). This rule fires the canonical succedent variant starting from the 2nd (2,3,4,5,6,7,8). The full classical form spans any panaphara/apoklima start; the additional starts are surfaced as separate variants in a future expansion.
Chakra (wheel) Akriti: all 7 grahas in odd houses (1+3+5+7+9+11). Confers cyclical fortune, wheel-of-fate themes — kingship per BPHS.
Samudra (ocean) Akriti: all 7 grahas in even houses (2+4+6+8+10+12). Confers vast wealth, deep resourcefulness — "ocean of fortune" per BPHS.
Damini (rope-like) Akriti: all 7 grahas in 7 alternate houses (broadly the upachaya + dharma houses 3+5+7+9+11). Confers binding-disciplinary professions (judges, administrators).
Padma (lotus) Akriti: all 7 grahas in the four kendras (1+4+7+10). Confers complete kendra-bala — supreme stability, regal status. Distinct from the Lotus-named yogas in other categories.
Vapi (well/water-tank) Akriti: all 7 grahas in the four panaparas (2+5+8+11). Confers wealth-accumulation, deep-resource professions, hidden treasures.
Lagna-lord and 4th-lord exchange signs. Confers domestic happiness, vehicles, and stable home life linked directly to self.
Lagna-lord and 7th-lord exchange signs. Confers strong partnership and marital bond — self and spouse mirror each other.
Lagna-lord and 10th-lord exchange. The strongest career-identity yoga — self and karma are inseparable; status defines the native.
Exchange between home (4th) and partnership (7th) — confers harmonious domestic-marital integration.
Exchange between sukha (4th) and karma (10th) — kendra-axis exchange. Confers professional eminence supported by domestic stability.
Exchange between purva-punya (5th) and partnership (7th). Confers fortunate marriage and harmonious progeny.
Trikona-Kendra exchange (5th-10th) — Dharma-Karmadhipati Yoga. One of the strongest classical Raja Yogas; intelligence and authority compound each other.
Kendra-axis exchange (7th-10th). Confers professional success through partnership and reputation through associates.
Trikona-Kendra exchange (9th-10th) — the canonical Dharma-Karmadhipati Yoga (mirror of 5-10). The "fortune in profession" yoga — career rises directly with dharma.

Dusthana exchange (6-8). Threatens chronic conflict, debt, and health crises — the two affliction-houses reinforce each other. Distinct from Vipareeta where ONE dusthana lord goes into ANOTHER and produces protection — here the EXCHANGE keeps both lords in dusthanas.
Dusthana exchange (6-12). Threatens long-term debts and dissipating expenses — disease (6) drains income; expenses (12) generate disputes (6).
Dusthana exchange (8-12). Threatens isolation, hidden affairs, and chronic dissolution of resources. Often associated with reclusive or institutional life.

Jupiter and Mars conjunct. Combination of wisdom (Guru) and energy (Mangal) — confers leadership grounded in dharma. Mixed nature: dharma + assertion can manifest as either righteous authority or rigid combat.
Jupiter and Venus conjunct — the two great benefics together. Confers wealth, refinement, and high education. Both teachers (Guru of devas, Guru of asuras) unite their wisdom.
Saturn and Mars conjunct — natural enemies forced together. Threatens accidents, surgeries, conflicts with authority, and chronic frustration. Mars's heat clashes with Saturn's cold.
Sun conjunct Rahu — solar eclipse imprint. Threatens authority figures (especially father), self-confidence, and spiritual identity. Co-detected with `GRAHAN_DOSHA`.
Moon conjunct Rahu — lunar eclipse imprint. Threatens emotional stability, mother, and intuition. Manifests as anxiety, sleep disturbances, and unstable mind.
Moon conjunct Ketu — south-node lunar imprint. Pulls the mind toward isolation, detachment, or spiritual withdrawal — sometimes manifesting as introversion, sometimes as renunciation tendency.
Lagna flanked by benefics in 2nd and 12th — kartari (scissors) of benefic protection around the self. Confers physical wellness and protection from external malefic influence.
Lagna flanked by malefics in 2nd and 12th — kartari (scissors) of malefic affliction around the self. Threatens physical wellness, peer influence, and psychological pressure.

Jupiter, Venus, and Mercury all in 1/2/4/5/7/9/10 (kendras + trikonas + dhana). Phaladeepika's strong-tier formulation adds 'at least one in own/exalted dignity' — that supplementary dignity check is handled by the engine's strength-scoring on the involved benefics rather than the presence predicate (so the yoga still fires at full structural coverage; dignity modulates strength). Distinct from the SARASWATI_BENEFIC_KENDRA rule in `chandra.yogas` which requires all three specifically in kendras (no trikona admission).
Lords of 5th and 6th both in kendras. The "conch shell" yoga — confers fame, longevity, and good fortune through service to dharma. Phaladeepika lists this among the high Raja Yogas.

Variant of Hamsa Mahapurusha — Jupiter occupies a house that is BOTH a kendra AND a trikona (only the 1st house qualifies). The "kendra-trikona Hamsa" — strongest classical placement of Jupiter conferring wisdom, status, and dharma simultaneously.

"Unbroken empire" yoga: Jupiter in a kendra plus 2nd-lord or 11th-lord placed in Lagna or another kendra. Confers vast and lasting authority — the highest classical Raja Yoga indicating sovereign status.
Lord of labha (gains) falling into the dusthana of debts/disputes (6th). Threatens financial loss and chronic indebtedness. Cancelled when 11th lord is in a kendra elsewhere.
Lord of gains in the 8th — sudden ruptures in income, financial setbacks through unexpected events.
Lord of gains in the 12th (loss/expenditure). Earnings dissipate before accumulation; chronic outflow exceeds inflow.
Malefics simultaneously in Lagna and 7th — afflicts both self (1st) and partnership/spouse (7th). Threatens marital discord and self-image conflicts.
Saturn conjunct Moon — "poison" yoga. Saturnine restriction blocks the Moon's emotional flow; threatens depression, isolation, and chronic mental fatigue. Cancelled when Jupiter occupies a kendra.
Lagna-lord (self) in the 6th house of disease, debt, and conflict. Threatens the body and self-confidence. Cancelled by Jupiter in a kendra or 6th-lord in a kendra (Vipareeta-style protection).
Lagna-lord in the 8th house of longevity, transformation, and hidden affairs. Threatens chronic health problems and unstable identity unless fortified by aspect from Jupiter.
Lagna-lord in the 12th house of loss, expenditure, and foreign lands. Native often lives away from birthplace; energies dissipate unless 12th has benefic support.
6th-lord (disease, debt, enemies) occupying Lagna. Threatens chronic ill-health and self-undermining patterns; the "enemy in the self" classical configuration.
8th-lord (longevity-affliction, hidden affairs) in Lagna. Threatens body, vitality, and reputation through unseen forces. Strongly modulated by 8th-lord's own dignity.
